questions.prompt: Why did James have to try out for the dragon?
choices: James had forgotten the name of the play.
Six other children put their hands up too.
Anna wanted to paint the dragon costume.
questions.answer: Six other children put their hands up too.
questions.evidenceText: James put his hand straight up. "I want to be the dragon!" Six other children put their hands up too. They would all have to try out.

questions.prompt: What helped James after he forgot his line?
choices: The audience told him the words.
Anna gave him a thumbs up.
questions.answer: Anna gave him a thumbs up.
questions.rationale: Anna's thumbs-up comes just after James forgets his line; on the next page he takes a deep breath and gives his roar, so her encouragement helped him continue.
questions.evidenceText: He forgot his first line. The hall went silent. Anna was watching from the side. She caught his eye and gave him a thumbs up.

supportingEvidence.evidenceText: James took a deep breath. He thought of his best roar. Then he let it out — the biggest, loudest roar he had ever done.

questions.prompt: How did the audience respond at the end?
choices: They asked for a new play.
questions.evidenceText: At the very end, everyone stood and clapped. James and Anna walked to the front of the stage and bowed together.
